newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia June palm oil output seen little changed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia June palm oil output seen little changed.

text.p: Malaysian crude palm oil output in June is estimated to have fallen slightly from May's 790,640 tonnes, according to plantation houses surveyed on Friday.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is scheduled to release the June crop data on July 15.
"June's output could fall by two percent or remain unchanged," one plantation firm official said.
"Output in June could be affected by the dry weather, particularly in East Malaysian state of Sabah," the official said.
"Crops are seen ripening and there isn't much rain to help with the ripening. Harvest could be delayed because of the dry weather, which will drag on until end of this month," he said.
Ivan Wong, a private crop forecaster, is scheduled to release his latest crop data on July 14. Wong had earlier projected output in June at 785,000 tonnes.
Traders have estimated end-June stocks at 790,000 to 795,000 tonnes against PORLA's end-May 711,841 tonnes.
Exports in June were estimated at between 595,000 and 615,000 tonnes against PORLA's 626,606 tonnes in May.
